headings.usage: Use tight letter spacing (tracking-tight) for Gates overview headings and Higgins alerts. Avoid generic system fonts for top-level headers to maintain an authoritative brand voice.

body.usage: Use for explanations, file details, device logs, and Higgins's conversational text. High legibility is critical for security findings.

monospace.usage: Use for displaying specific file names, paths, app package names, and raw permission logs.

primary.description: Deep Obsidian background for the app to emphasize focus and security.

visual_enhancers.borders: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1) for cards to provide structural layout. Hard edges with max 8px border-radius.
visual_enhancers.shadows: Minimal ambient shadows. Use crisp, high-contrast separation.
visual_enhancers.textures: Subtle noise overlay (opacity 0.02) to avoid pure digital flatness.
visual_enhancers.glassmorphism: Only for sticky headers or Higgins modal popups, using a heavily blurred background with a 1px border. DO NOT use completely transparent backgrounds over scrollable content.

GateCard.layout: Row-based or dense 2-column grid. Left-aligned content.

states.Ready to check: Show a subdued outline pill or badge (grey).

HigginsBlock.style: Visually distinct container, perhaps with a subtle blue/indigo left-border treatment to indicate 'Assistant/Higgins' voice.
HigginsBlock.buttons: Actionable buttons must contrast strongly (e.g., solid white button with black text for primary actions like 'Open Settings').

StatusBadge.description: Pill component representing assessment statuses (e.g., Safe, Warning, Tampered).
StatusBadge.rules: Must have an explicit icon alongside text for accessibility.

grids_and_layouts.GatesOverview: Dense layout displaying all 10 Gates. Mobile-first list or 2-column grid if horizontal space allows. Generous spacing (p-6) inside each card to prevent text collision.
grids_and_layouts.DetailScreens: Reuse existing /file and /device layouts, but ensure they inject the new Higgins remediation blocks natively in the flow.
grids_and_layouts.Alignment: Left-align dense content. Never center-align paragraphs, explanations, or security logs.

motion.status_indicators: Subtle scale and opacity pulse for 'Active' monitoring states.
motion.transitions: Use specific transform and opacity transitions (e.g., duration 200ms ease-in-out) for navigating into File/Device specific screens. Avoid global 'transition: all'.

accessibility.contrast: Ensure APCA/WCAG AA compliance. Normal text 4.5:1, large text 3:1.
accessibility.test_ids: Every interactive element MUST include a data-testid attribute (e.g., data-testid="file-gate-select-button", data-testid="higgins-remediate-btn").
accessibility.labels: Do not rely on color alone to convey security status; always include text labels or explicit icons.

media.icons: Use Phosphor Icons (or Expo vector equivalents like Lucide) for crisp, professional iconography.

instructions_to_main_agent: You are building for an Expo React Native app. Adapt the Tailwind/CSS terminology to React Native StyleSheet or NativeWind if used.
Integrate 'File Gate' and 'Device Gate' into the main Gates overview. The overview MUST contain exactly ten Gates.
Ensure the statuses are strictly labeled as 'Ready to check' for manual tasks, and 'Active' for ongoing monitors. Do not automatically scan dormant files/apps without triggering.
When assessing files, neutralise source bias. Host being 'Google Drive' != Safe.
When assessing device, a dormant app must not be treated as harmless merely because inactive.
Apollo protection health must be assessed. Only report tampering with explicit evidence.
Higgins component must present findings, provide remediation steps (e.g., 'Open Settings'), and include functionality to re-check the state.
Reuse the existing `/file` and `/device` routes where applicable.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: Do not converge toward generic 'AI slop' aesthetics. Make the app feel authoritative, tactical, and distinct.
No generic centered layouts for data-heavy views. Align content structurally.
Create depth through 1px borders and layered z-index, not muddy gradients.
DO NOT apply universal transitions (transition: all).
DO NOT use completely transparent backgrounds for overlays, dropdowns, or sticky headers.
Include data-testid attributes on ALL buttons, inputs, and interactive components.
NEVER use emoji characters as icons.
